patch.value: GH-1518: recover provably dead same-host item-lock owners before TTL expiry

https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1518 reports on published 2026.10.20/Linux/plain non-Git trackers that a killed public-SDK lock holder leaves an item unavailable for the full 3600-second TTL. Later update/comments calls and force recovery refuse after the normal wait, while health counts the receipt as active. This is reporter evidence; current-head reproduction and implementation remain pending. The new boundary is provable same-host process death before TTL expiry, rather than expired-lock GC, live-lock throughput or safe ownership publication.

Add owned-sandbox SDK and CLI crash recovery tests. Record enough host/process-start identity to distinguish a dead original owner from PID reuse, foreign hosts, EPERM/unknown liveness and legacy receipts. Reclaim only with positive proof through the existing token-validated stale-cleanup gate, preserving initialization and single-winner takeover invariants. Keep unknown/live owners and malformed/partial receipts conservative. Health, GC and conflict recovery should consistently expose liveness/staleness and an actionable actual command; record recovery provenance without losing acknowledged writes.
A provably dead same-host owner cannot block writes for an hour, while live, reused, foreign-host or unknown process identities remain protected.
